trials.objective: Start with heat = 80 and alarm = "OFF". Write an if statement: if heat > 50:, set alarm = "ON" and print("Shield up!").

starterCode.explorer:
heat = 80
alarm = "OFF"
# Notice the colon : at the end and 4 spaces of indent below!
if heat > 50:
    alarm = "ON"
    # Now print "Shield up!" (keep the 4-space indent!)
starterCode.standard:
heat = 80
alarm = "OFF"
# If heat > 50, set alarm = "ON" and print("Shield up!")
starterCode.challenge:
heat = 80
alarm = "OFF"
# When heat > 50, switch alarm to "ON" and print "Shield up!".

trials.referenceSolution:
heat = 80
alarm = "OFF"
if heat > 50:
    alarm = "ON"
    print("Shield up!")
trials.testCode:

assert OUTPUT.strip() == "Shield up!", f'Expected "Shield up!", got {OUTPUT.strip()!r}'

hints.tier1_nudge: Pip points at the colon: 'Every if line ends with : and every line inside the if block is indented 4 spaces!'
hints.tier3_walkthrough:

trials.title: True or False? (Your First Boolean Box)
trials.storyPrompt: In Python, a Boolean is a special yes-or-no value: either `True` or `False` (always capital T or F, and NO quotes!). A comparison like `lava_temp > 500` automatically turns into `True` or `False`!
trials.objective: Set lava_temp = 850 and create a boolean variable is_too_hot = lava_temp > 500, then print(is_too_hot).

starterCode.explorer:
lava_temp = 850
# Compare lava_temp to 500 using > to get True or False:
is_too_hot = lava_temp >

starterCode.standard:
lava_temp = 850
# Set is_too_hot using a comparison with 500, then print(is_too_hot)
starterCode.challenge: # Store 850 in lava_temp, set is_too_hot to whether lava_temp > 500, and print(is_too_hot).

trials.referenceSolution:
lava_temp = 850
is_too_hot = lava_temp > 500
print(is_too_hot)
trials.testCode:
assert lava_temp == 850
assert is_too_hot is True, f'Expected is_too_hot to be True, got {is_too_hot!r}'
assert OUTPUT.strip() == 'True', f'Expected printed True, got {OUTPUT.strip()!r}'

hints.tier1_nudge: Pip fans himself: 'lava_temp > 500 asks Python a yes/no question and puts True into the is_too_hot box!'
hints.tier2_pattern:

trials.objective: Start with water_level = 30. Write an if / else statement: if water_level >= 50, set bridge = "COOL"; else, set bridge = "HOT". Then print(bridge).

starterCode.challenge:

# Set bridge to "COOL" if water_level >= 50, otherwise "HOT", then print(bridge).

trials.testCode:
assert bridge == "HOT", f'Expected bridge == "HOT" for water_level 30, got {bridge!r}'
assert OUTPUT.strip() == "HOT", f'Expected printed "HOT", got {OUTPUT.strip()!r}'

hints.tier1_nudge: Pip fans the steam: 'Since 30 is NOT >= 50, Python skips the if block and runs the else: block!'
hints.tier3_walkthrough:

trials.objective: Start with gems = 7 and door = "SHUT". Write an if statement checking if gems == 7: set door = "OPEN" and print("Click!").

starterCode.explorer:

door = "SHUT"
# If gems == 7, set door = "OPEN" and print("Click!")
starterCode.challenge:

door = "SHUT"
# Open door and print "Click!" when gems equals 7.

gems = 7
door = "SHUT"

trials.testCode:

assert OUTPUT.strip() == "Click!", f'Expected "Click!", got {OUTPUT.strip()!r}'
